name: Magnet-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The card is pulled furthest toward the cursor while all three pieces stay in view.

tagline: Elements drift toward the cursor, then settle back when it leaves.
summary: Wraps anything so it leans toward the pointer when it comes within a set distance, scaled by a strength you choose, and eases back to rest once the pointer moves away.
appearance: Three items sit in a row on black: a white pill reading "Hover me", a square outlined tile holding a white sparkle, and a small outlined card with a title and hint line. When the pointer comes near, an item slides a little toward it.
behaviour: A pointer listener measures each item against its centre plus a padding zone; while the pointer is inside that zone the item translates toward it in proportion to the distance, and once outside it eases back to its spot.
demo_content: A button reading "Hover me", a sparkle tile and a card titled "Magnetic card" with "Move your cursor near me"
search_phrases: cards drawn to the mouse pointer
nearby items pull toward the cursor
springy pull when the mouse comes close
playful cursor attraction on a hero
objects that drift to the pointer
use_when: A hero or feature row should feel alive and invite the pointer without asking for a click.
avoid_when: Touch devices, where there is no hover, and dense layouts where items shifting feels unstable.
customise: Wrap any element as children; padding radius, magnet strength, disabled state, active and inactive transitions and wrapper class names are props.
weight_why: A window pointer listener and one transform transition per wrapped item.

a11y.note: The pull is pointer-only with no reduced-motion fallback, and every instance listens to window pointer moves.

issues: The gaps between items change as each one moves, so the row visibly loosens while the pointer is near.
polish_why: Movement is smooth and restrained; the shifting gaps make the row feel loose.
